title: Pollo alla Cacciatora
subtitle: Chicken braised with tomatoes, olives, capers, and white wine
excerpt: Chicken thighs cooked low and slow in a robust tomato sauce with olives and capers. The sauce reduces to something deeply savoury. Serve with bread or polenta.
sourceNotes: Hunter-style Italian chicken dish, widely made across central and northern Italy with regional variations.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooked chicken and sauce together. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat gently.
recipe.batchNotes: Use two pans to brown extra thighs. The sauce works well at double quantity.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The flavour deepens overnight. Make a day ahead and reheat gently on the hob.

content.text: Cacciatora means hunter-style. The chicken is browned first, then braised in a thick tomato and wine sauce. The olives and capers go in at the end so they keep their edge. Do not rush the initial browning step.

Season the chicken thighs on both sides. Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over a medium-high heat. Brown the thighs skin-side down for 5 minutes until the skin is golden. Turn and brown for 2 minutes more. Remove and set aside.
Pour off most of the fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and oregano and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the white wine and let it simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the tinned tomatoes and break them up. Return the chicken to the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered on a low heat for 40 minutes until the sauce is thick and the chicken is cooked through.
Add the olives and capers. Stir and cook for 5 minutes more. Taste and adjust seasoning. Scatter over parsley if using.

items.symptom: The chicken skin is soft, not golden.
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough before the chicken went in.
items.fix: Make sure the oil is shimmering before adding the thighs. Do not move them for the first 4 minutes.

items.symptom: The sauce is too thin after 40 minutes.
items.cause: The pan was covered during cooking or the heat was very low.
items.fix: Cook uncovered on a medium heat for another 10 minutes to reduce the sauce.

items.symptom: The dish tastes too sharp from the capers.
items.cause: Salt-packed capers were used without rinsing.
items.fix: Rinse capers well before using. If the dish is already sharp, add a pinch of sugar to balance it.
